cse-2021-2-cs-43.approach: Check Coffman conditions: the scheme lets a requester forcibly take a resource from its owner, so "no preemption" is broken and deadlock cannot occur. But victims are restarted and can be preempted again and again.

steps.title: Deadlock
steps.body: A process requesting a held resource never waits: it terminates the owner, takes the resource, and restarts the owner. Since nobody waits holding resources, the circular-wait/no-preemption conditions cannot both hold — **deadlock cannot occur** (A true). Everything happens under the global lock \`L\`, and an instance still has a single owner at any time — **mutual exclusion is preserved** (D false).

steps.title: Livelock and starvation
steps.body: P1 holds $R_1$, P2 holds $R_2$. P1 requests $R_2$ → kills/restarts P2. P2 restarts, grabs $R_2$ back, requests $R_1$ → kills/restarts P1, and so on. Both keep running but neither finishes — **livelock** (B true). Likewise one unlucky process can be terminated every time it gets going while others finish — **starvation** (C true).

optionAnalysis.reason: Requests are satisfied by preempting the owner, so no process ever waits for a held resource; deadlock is prevented.
Two processes can keep terminating and restarting each other without progress.
A process can be chosen as the victim repeatedly and never complete.
Ownership changes only under the global lock, and the old owner releases everything first; at most one owner per instance at any time.

pitfalls: Confusing "preempting a resource" with "violating mutual exclusion" — the resource is handed over, never shared.
cse-2021-2-cs-43.verification: Coffman check: hold-and-wait and no-preemption are both broken (no one waits; holders are preempted), so deadlock is impossible.

Dependent EX starts right after the producer's EX. EX lengths: ADD 1, MUL 2. I1's EX is in cycle 3; then EX cycles run back-to-back:

- I1: EX 3, WB 5.
- each MUL: EX 2 cycles + MEM + WB = 4 cycles after the previous WB; each ADD: 3 cycles.

$$5 + 4\cdot 4 + 3 \cdot 3 = 5 + 16 + 9 = 30 \text{ cycles}$$
